candidates.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
candidates.title_zh: T2-Z：面向机器人世界模型的环境潜变量测试时优化
candidates.abstract: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.
candidates.summary_zh: 为机器人世界模型引入可学习环境潜变量以条件化预测：训练时交替优化模型与潜变量，测试时冻结模型、仅用少量交互优化新潜变量，在 7 个仿真与 4 项真机任务上降低预测误差并提升动作成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出测试时环境潜变量优化框架 T2-Z，无监督捕获摩擦、质量、规则等环境变化，并能从单条交互轨迹快速推断潜变量。

ai_review.reason: 面向机器人世界模型的环境潜变量测试时优化，直接服务物理智能与动作条件预测。

candidates.title: Perceive, Predict, and Plan: a Unified World Action Model for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: 感知、预测与规划：面向第一视角灵巧操作的统一世界动作模型
candidates.abstract: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/
candidates.summary_zh: 提出P3-WAM统一世界动作模型，通过感知、预测、规划三种模式学习3D感知、动作条件预测和目标导向规划，集成3D动作表示与视频扩散Transformer，在多个数据集上超越专用基线。
candidates.contribution_zh: 统一感知、预测、规划三种模式，通过混合Transformer架构将结构化3D动作表示融入预训练视频扩散模型，实现动作条件视频预测与目标导向操作规划。

ai_review.reason: 直接相关具身智能与机器人世界模型，提出统一世界动作模型，应收录。

candidates.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
candidates.title_zh: GeoState：学习视角解耦几何状态用于3D世界建模
candidates.abstract: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/
candidates.summary_zh: 提出视角解耦几何表示，将场景状态演化与相机观测分离。场景tokenizer聚合多视角几何基础模型特征，自回归世界模型预测未来状态，相机运动单独建模，支持指定相机解码。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将场景动态与相机变化解耦，提升预测世界状态的可预测性与跨视角查询一致性，并可零样本泛化。

ai_review.reason: 属于机器人世界模型与动作条件预测方向，几何状态解耦直接服务物理智能。

candidates.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
candidates.abstract: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

candidates.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient
candidates.title_zh: Velox：空间记忆让世界模型更高效
candidates.abstract: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry. Velox represents historical blocks as camera frustum slabs with depth intervals and obtains current-block depth through recency-priority multiwarp. For well-covered regions, frustum slab overlap softly modulates each layer's model-derived block importance. Uncovered regions retain the model-derived route without geometric bias. The fixed token-block granularity matches FlashAttention-style tiled execution and reduces the attention term that grows with rollout length. Frustum slab construction runs asynchronously with denoising on the same H200. At chunk 48, Velox accelerates attention by $4.36\times$ and denoising by $2.43\times$. On the full 158-case WBench navigation split, it remains within 0.15 API-free average points of dense LingBot-Fast-Cam. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/velox/ for more details.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出免训练的注意力路由 Velox，利用流式几何中的相机视锥板对应关系进行区域级上下文选择，将历史块表示为带深度区间的视锥板，加速长视频世界模型的多块生成，在 WBench 导航任务上保持精度。
candidates.contribution_zh: 免训练注意路由，用视锥板几何做区域级 KV 选择，降低随 rollout 增长的注意力开销，提升交互式视频世界模型效率。

ai_review.reason: 面向交互式视频世界模型，用空间几何加速长序列生成，直接服务物理智能仿真与规划。

candidates.title: REKI: Registering Knowledge in VLAs
candidates.title_zh: REKI：为视觉语言动作模型注入知识寄存器
candidates.abstract: We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots, and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer. REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: https://github.com/kyutai-labs/reki.
candidates.summary_zh: REKI 是仅用公开数据预训练的 2.4B 视觉语言动作模型，由视觉语言模型加流匹配动作专家构成，并在动作专家中引入少数寄存器 token 作为低成本记忆，在 LIBERO-Plus、RoboTwin、RoboCasa365 及真机上提升成功率并抑制姿态振荡。
candidates.contribution_zh: 以更小模型取得接近两倍规模模型的性能，提出用寄存器 token 缓存 VLM 输出形成策略短时记忆，并开源数据、训练、推理与权重。

ai_review.reason: 公开数据训练的2.4B视觉语言动作模型，含动作专家与记忆机制，直接服务机器人操作，属收录范围。

candidates.title: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: FastVLA：面向高效视觉-语言-动作模型的任务条件化与时间自适应视觉Token压缩
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts end-to-end latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.
candidates.summary_zh: FastVLA：无需训练、任务感知且时间自适应的视觉Token压缩方法，通过任务到视觉注意力评分重要性并动态调整压缩率。在VLA模型和真实机器人上减少计算延迟，保持成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出任务感知、时间自适应的免训练视觉Token压缩，提升VLA推理效率。

ai_review.reason: 直接服务物理智能的VLA模型效率优化，属动作接地。

candidates.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
candidates.abstract: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

candidates.title: Plans Are Not Executions: Adapting Frozen World-Model Planners to Controller-Induced Execution Shift
candidates.title_zh: 计划并非执行：将冻结世界模型规划器适配到控制器引起的执行偏移
candidates.abstract: World-model planners evaluate candidate trajectories by predicting their future consequences, implicitly relying on the plan-to-motion relationship learned during training. At deployment, a different downstream controller may execute the same planned trajectory differently, creating a planning-execution gap between the frozen model's imagined future and actual execution. A natural remedy is to replace the planned trajectory with its predicted or observed execution. However, we find that better execution fidelity does not necessarily yield better decisions: directly substituting predicted execution trajectories yields only a 0.048 PDMS improvement across 10 unseen controller configurations, far smaller than the gain from our proposed adaptation. This suggests a semantic mismatch between a planned trajectory, which serves as a reference for downstream control, and an executed trajectory, which already describes the resulting post-controller motion. We introduce ExecutionBridge, which infers controller-specific execution characteristics from planned-executed trajectory pairs and uses them to adapt the native ego latent rollout while keeping the original planned trajectory unchanged. The planner, world model, and reward head remain frozen. On NAVSIM, ExecutionBridge consistently improves planning across unseen controller configurations and multiple frozen world-model planners, with substantially larger gains in challenging driving scenes where execution mismatch more strongly affects candidate evaluation.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文研究世界模型规划器更换下游控制器时的规划-执行差距，发现直接替换执行轨迹提升有限。提出ExecutionBridge从计划-执行对推断控制器特性，适配冻结模型的潜变量推演，在NAVSIM未见控制器配置上稳定提升规划。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出ExecutionBridge，从计划-执行对推断控制器执行特性，在冻结规划器与世界模型下适配自我潜变量推演，提升跨控制器规划。

ai_review.reason: 提出适配冻结世界模型规划器以缩小控制器导致规划-执行差距，属具身/驾驶世界模型规划，建议收录。

candidates.title: VeriVLA: Adaptive Test-Time Verification for Flow-Based VLAs with Latent World Models
candidates.title_zh: VeriVLA：基于潜在世界模型的流式VLA自适应测试时验证
candidates.abstract: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.
candidates.summary_zh: 针对流式VLA策略的随机性，提出无需训练的双轴触发机制检测关键状态，并用JEPA潜在世界模型对候选动作块排序，在真实与仿真操作任务中提升成功率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出训练无关的触发机制与JEPA潜在世界模型验证器，无需像素重建即可对候选动作块排序，显著提升操作成功率。

ai_review.reason: 面向流式VLA的测试时验证，用JEPA潜在世界模型对动作块排序，属具身智能与动作条件预测。

candidates.title: TS-WAM: Temporal Latent Actions and World-Action Coupling for Vision-Language Robot Control
candidates.title_zh: TS-WAM：面向视觉-语言机器人控制的时间潜在动作与世界-动作耦合
candidates.abstract: Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. These limitations hinder learning from action-free videos and can encourage overfitting to demonstration conditions, weakening generalization and robustness. We present TS-WAM, a lightweight Teacher-Student World-Action Model that addresses these challenges through self-supervised temporal learning and explicit future prediction. Its vlm-jepa framework learns from heterogeneous data, including robot demonstrations and action-free human videos, using an EMA target branch without requiring a separately trained external teacher. By coupling vlm-jepa with delta-lwm, TS-WAM learns to predict latent actions from the current observation and instruction and uses them to predict future visual features that guide action generation at inference. A unified end-to-end training architecture jointly optimizes temporal representation learning, visual dynamics, and robot control without a separate latent-action or world-model pretraining stage. The EMA target branch is removed at inference, keeping the deployed policy lightweight. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv, together with real-world manipulation experiments on Franka Research 3 and RevoTron, demonstrate that TS-WAM achieves strong manipulation performance, generalization, and robustness.
candidates.summary_zh: TS-WAM用教师-学生架构从机器人演示和无动作人类视频中自监督学习时间潜在动作，预测未来视觉特征以指导VLA动作生成，在LIBERO和真实机器人上验证泛化与鲁棒性。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出轻量教师-学生世界-动作模型，统一优化时间表征、视觉动态与机器人控制，无需独立预训练阶段。

ai_review.reason: 提出TS-WAM，用VLM-JEPA与Delta-LWM耦合学习潜在动作并预测未来视觉特征，直接服务机器人控制。

candidates.title: What Should Robot Policies Learn to Predict? Rethinking Supervision Targets in Vision-Language-Action Learning
candidates.title_zh: 机器人策略应学习预测什么？重新思考视觉-语言-动作学习中的监督目标
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文提出统一VLA框架，用双流MMDiT和样本级路由器将训练样本显式分配给动作预测或辅助目标，在LIBERO、CALVIN及四项真机任务中比较潜动作与未来视觉监督。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出显式监督分配框架，系统比较潜动作与未来视觉目标，证明固定预算下辅助监督可优于纯动作训练，并揭示不同目标的表征侧重。

provenance.source_comment: 26 pages, 8 figures. Haitao Shen and Hanyu Liu contributed equally

ai_review.reason: 研究VLA策略监督目标分配与机器人动作学习直接相关，属具身智能范围。

candidates.title: CoWorld Reasoner: Agentic Multimodal Reasoning with the Evolving Video World Model-Driven Harness
candidates.abstract: As Vision-Language Models (VLMs) advance, they are increasingly expected to perform spatiotemporal reasoning over motion, actions, and view changes beyond what the input images show. Video World Models (VWMs) provide a natural unified engine for visual imagination by generating task-relevant visual content as additional evidence. However, existing approaches typically invoke a VWM through fixed pipelines centered on a predefined form of visual imagination, such as novel-view synthesis. To support flexible visual imagination for diverse reasoning tasks, we introduce CoWorld Reasoner, an agentic framework that uses a VWM as a unified visual reasoning engine. Its Video World Model-Driven Harness exposes multiple visual operations through tools and uses skills to guide the VLM in deciding whether to imagine, selecting an operation, constructing a generation request, and interpreting the resulting visual evidence. We further introduce VLM-VWM Harness Co-Evolution, which jointly revises tools, skills, and execution code based on execution feedback while keeping both model weights fixed. Across seven benchmarks spanning spatial intelligence, temporal and causal reasoning, and perceptual reasoning, CoWorld Reasoner outperforms direct reasoning with the same VLM. The strongest variant improves on all seven benchmarks, including relative accuracy gains of 11.8% on MMSI and 13.0% on ERQA, and outperforms all five evolving baselines using the same backbone across five benchmarks.

candidates.title: MAIA: Anticipating Interaction Anomalies in Contact-Rich Manipulation via Multimodal World Models
candidates.title_zh: MAIA：通过多模态世界模型预见富接触操作中的交互异常
candidates.abstract: Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. Yet most monitoring methods are reactive, identifying anomalies only after they become observable. Anticipating such anomalies is challenging because visual observations only partially reveal physical interaction, while planned actions describe intended motion rather than their actual physical consequences. We address this problem with MAIA, a multimodal framework for anomaly anticipation. Its vision-action-force world model learns nominal interaction dynamics and predicts the visual and force responses of planned actions, while a lightweight anomaly head predicts impending interaction anomalies. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce CRIA, a real-world multimodal dataset of 2,852 trajectories spanning 18 contact-rich manipulation tasks, with frame-level annotations of anomaly onset and evolution. Experiments on both seen and novel tasks show that MAIA achieves more accurate anomaly discrimination than representative baselines while providing earlier warnings, with bACC scores of 0.765 and 0.710 and median anticipation lead times of 28.0 and 25.1 steps, respectively. Moreover, using these predictions for anomaly-aware action selection improves end-to-end task success from 52.6% to 61.5% without retraining the underlying manipulation policy. These results highlight the value of modeling future physical consequences for proactive anomaly anticipation.
candidates.summary_zh: MAIA 用视觉-动作-力世界模型预测计划动作的视觉与力响应，配轻量异常头提前预警；构建 CRIA 真实数据集（2852 轨迹、18 任务），判别更准更早，任务成功率 52.6%→61.5%。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出视觉-动作-力多模态世界模型实现主动式交互异常前瞻，并发布 CRIA 富接触操作数据集。

ai_review.reason: 富接触操作的多模态世界模型与交互异常前瞻，直接服务机器人物理智能。

candidates.title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models
candidates.title_zh: 潜世界模型中的内在动态学习
candidates.abstract: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. We investigate the connection between action predictability, defined as the ability to reconstruct an action from consecutive latent states, and the preservation of intrinsic dynamics. Our central hypothesis is that encouraging action predictability discourages representations from discarding the distinctions between different actions and their consequences. We provide two complementary forms of evidence for this connection. Theoretically, we derive a positive lower bound on squared inverse prediction error when the encoder merges distinguishable outcomes of different actions from the same state and appearance, and show that forward prediction can still be exact on those transitions. Empirically, controlled appearance-diversity comparisons, supervision interventions, and latent probes support the role of action prediction in preserving control-relevant transition information. We instantiate action predictability with Concat IDM, which predicts actions from concatenated latent states and updates the shared encoder using action labels already available in offline trajectories, without changing the test-time planner. Across three independent training runs on Push-T with 24 appearances, Concat IDM increases planning success from 9.1% to 77.2%; its paired improvement is 52.9 percentage points larger than that observed with a single appearance. Together, these findings support action predictability as an inductive bias toward intrinsic dynamics and demonstrate the practical benefits of Concat IDM for latent planning under visual diversity.

candidates.contribution_zh: 提出动作可预测性理论下界与Concat IDM，证明并验证其保留控制相关动态，在多外观Push-T上将规划成功率从9.1%提升至77.2%。

candidates.title: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: 面向基于流的视觉-语言-动作模型的多教师在线策略蒸馏
candidates.abstract: Specialized vision-language-action (VLA) policies acquire strong domain-specific skills, yet consolidating these skills into one shared policy remains challenging. On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher knowledge on inputs induced by the student, addressing the distribution mismatch encountered during deployment. For flow-based VLAs, this mismatch arises at two levels: environment observations and intermediate action-generation states. We propose a two-level on-policy distillation framework that couples student-driven environment interaction with teacher velocity supervision along student-generated action flow trajectories. Frozen domain specialists jointly supervise one student. After each update, the student collects new environment experience and generates fresh action-flow trajectories. Starting from a joint supervised fine-tuning (SFT) initialization, Velocity Loss OPD yields absolute success-rate gains of 22.55% on LIBERO-40, 33.4% on CALVIN five-instruction sequences, and 22.6% on Meta-World MT50. Compared with Action Loss OPD and Teacher-rollout SFT, it achieves absolute success-rate gains of 6.4-9.5% on LIBERO-40, 9.7-18.3% on CALVIN, and 3.2-4.2% on Meta-World MT50. Analysis by sequence length further shows larger success-rate gains on longer CALVIN sequences. These results demonstrate effective multi-domain capability consolidation through two-level on-policy supervision, with a single student deployed across domains.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出两级在线策略蒸馏框架，将学生驱动的环境交互与教师速度监督结合，把多个领域专家能力整合进单一基于流的VLA策略，在LIBERO-40、CALVIN与Meta-World MT50上成功率大幅提升。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出面向流式VLA的两级在线蒸馏与速度损失，实现多领域专家能力向单一策略的高效整合。

candidates.title: CarryOn: A Dual-Loop Harness for Personalized and Reliable Robot Assistance
candidates.title_zh: CarryOn：面向个性化可靠机器人助手的双环框架
candidates.abstract: While generalist vision-language-action (VLA) models have enabled diverse open-world manipulation, real-world robotic assistance requires two critical capabilities they currently lack: personalization and reliable execution. First, executing an instruction like "make me a sandwich" requires grounding subtask decomposition in persistent user preferences rather than relying on a single generic solution. Second, reliable deployment demands explainable safety assurance that proactively prevents hazards and gracefully recovers from occasional physical failures. To address these gaps, we present CarryOn, a dual-loop harness designed to augment a frozen VLA policy. The planning loop maintains persistent user-level and scene-level context that is continually grounded against new observations and revised through interaction, enabling personalized task selection and execution grounding across conversations and changing scenes. The execution loop actively supervises policy rollouts, shielding actions from predicted hazardous contact. When execution fails, the system invokes reusable control-based recovery skills that restore task progress and are refined through reflection on earlier failures. On a real robot and in simulation, CarryOn dispatches preference-consistent subtasks across users and scenes, reduces the violation rate of an already safety-finetuned VLA from 52.6% to 6.1%, and increases recovery success from 13% to 80% when refined skills are reused.
candidates.summary_zh: CarryOn为冻结VLA策略加装双环：规划环持久维护用户与场景上下文，实现个性化子任务分解；执行环监督动作、屏蔽危险接触，失败时调用可复用恢复技能。真机与仿真验证降低违规率并提升恢复率。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出双环框架增强冻结VLA：规划环实现个性化与场景接地，执行环提供安全屏蔽与可复用恢复技能；真机与仿真中显著降低危险违规率并提升恢复成功率。

candidates.title: Policy-Aligned Predictive Verification for Adaptive VLA Action-Chunk Execution
candidates.title_zh: 策略对齐预测验证用于自适应VLA动作块执行
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies generate action sequences that reduce repeated inference, but deciding how much of each sequence to execute is critical to task success. Existing adaptive methods make this decision using generation stability or prediction agreement, yet these signals do not establish whether executing a candidate prefix preserves the ability to complete the task. We introduce a policy-aligned predictive verifier (PAV) that anticipates the consequences of candidate action prefixes and evaluates their compatibility with successful continuation before execution. Rather than using future prediction to generate actions, our method evaluates existing proposals in the VLA's internal task-conditioned representation space. To learn local judgments from terminal task outcomes, we combine trajectory-level survival supervision with a localization prior that preserves useful behavior within failed rollouts. The resulting validity scores guide execution-horizon selection. Evaluations with pi_0 and pi_0.5 across LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world manipulation show improved success-query trade-offs. These findings point toward a different role for future prediction in robotics, using it to assess how far to trust a policy's proposed actions rather than to generate new ones.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出PAV，在VLA内部任务条件表征空间预测候选动作前缀后果，以其与成功续接的兼容性选择执行视界，改善成功率与查询权衡。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出策略对齐预测验证器，用轨迹级生存监督与定位先验学习动作前缀有效性评分，指导VLA执行视界选择，而非生成动作。

candidates.title: Fast-VLA: You Only Think Once for Robot Manipulation
candidates.title_zh: Fast-VLA：机器人操作只需思考一次
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies commonly place a multi-billion-parameter model inside the feedback loop, repeatedly recomputing task context whenever they predict a new action chunk. Yet task understanding changes far more slowly than the robot state. We introduce Fast-VLA, which invokes a frozen 4B VLM once per episode to contextualize the instruction and initial views as fixed, multi-layer key-value task memory. During execution, a lightweight online actor fuses learned time- and arm-indexed queries with current visual and proprioceptive feedback to form action queries. These queries retrieve task context from the fixed memory and predict action chunks without re-running the foundation model. Fast-VLA achieves 92.46% and 92.40% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean and Randomized, and 95.95% and 79.11% on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus evaluation. Against three continually conditioned baselines on the same hardware, it reduces RoboTwin amortized policy inference time by 10.9-17.1x and requires 1.22 GiB of post-prefill online resident memory. Task-memory swaps further show that the actor relies on episode-matched task memory. These results show that task context can be established once while closed-loop control remains responsive throughout execution. Project page: https://garfield-kh.github.io/FastVLA
candidates.summary_zh: 提出每回合仅调用一次冻结4B VLM构建键值任务记忆，在线轻量动作器融合视觉与本体反馈检索任务上下文，直接预测动作块，避免反复运行大模型。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将任务理解与闭环控制解耦，固定任务记忆加轻量在线动作器，实现高成功率与10倍以上推理加速。

candidates.title: From Optical Flow to Safety: Visual Safety Certification via Scale-Free Relative Motion
candidates.abstract: Safe autonomous navigation using monocular vision remains challenging because explicit obstacle states are not directly observable. This letter introduces a visual safety-certification paradigm that uses scale-free, depth-normalized relative motion encoded by monocular optical flow as the representation for collision-risk certification, without reconstructing obstacle position, velocity, geometry, or a metric world model. Unlike conventional optical-flow-based navigation approaches that rely on image motion to shape avoidance behavior, the proposed framework directly encodes collision-cone geometry and safety constraints in this relative-motion representation. An online Concurrent Learning observer estimates the normalized relative velocity and provides a computable estimation-error bound. This uncertainty is propagated into the collision cone through angular inflation and a monocular robot-footprint margin, yielding a Robust Vision-Based Collision Cone Control Barrier Function (RV-C$^3$BF). An optimal-decay CBF quadratic program minimally modifies the nominal control input to enforce the resulting robust safety constraint under the stated assumptions. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments on a TurtleBot3 in cluttered environments with static and dynamic obstacles demonstrate collision avoidance using only monocular vision and onboard proprioception, with the estimation-error bound containing the measured error in $98.3\%$ of simulation samples and the robot achieving collision-free navigation in $93$ of $100$ real-world trials.

candidates.title: LTM: Latent Transition Based In-Context Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering interactions that are no longer visible. We introduce Latent Transition Memory (LTM), which stores history as compact latent transitions between consecutive observations. Instantiated on $π_{0.5}$ as LTM-$π$, our method uses a frozen latent action encoder, a lightweight adapter, and causal KV caching for incremental inference without memory-specific semantic annotations or external reasoning-model calls. With DreamDojo transitions, LTM-$π$ achieves 58.54% success on RoboMME and 80.5% on LIBERO-Mem, performing best among baselines without external reasoning models or memory-specific annotations. Ablations support the contribution of transition content beyond temporal cues and the efficiency of delayed memory admission. Scaling RoboMME demonstrations tenfold improves success from 57.67% to 87.50%, while a Cup Swap diagnostic highlights the role of process supervision in temporal composition. Under a 200-token memory budget, success remains 84.00%, versus 87.50% without compression. Finally, real-robot counting success improves from 11.25% to 82.50%. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and efficiency of latent transition memory, highlighting its capacity for complex temporal information, bounded-context operation, and real-world robotic control.

candidates.title: Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Imagination
candidates.title_zh: 约束多智能体强化学习在想象中
candidates.abstract: Predicting cost in a multi-agent world model moves most constrained policy updates into imagination: the stronger model-free baseline needs $10$ to $20$ times CA-MAMBA's interactions on the median SMAC configuration, and CA-MAMBA earns $2.8$ to $12$ times the baselines' MAMuJoCo reward at equal budget. In controlled tests on one task per benchmark, pricing the model's cost advantages at parity more than halves a cost-blind learner's cost and meets a tight continuous-control limit the learned multiplier misses, suggesting the model's cost estimates are not the bottleneck.

candidates.title: VLA-$Δ$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: VLA-Δ：为视觉-语言-动作模型学习物理状态转移
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer semantic knowledge acquired through vision-language pretraining to robot control, achieving strong performance across various benchmarks. However, most VLAs directly map observations to demonstrated actions without explicit supervision of intermediate physical state changes, making them prone to overfitting observation-action correspondences. Some methods introduce intermediate reasoning or future-state prediction in language, visual, or latent spaces to guide action generation, but do not explicitly supervise the physical state transition itself. We therefore propose VLA-$Δ$, a general framework that uses physical changes between current and future states as explicit learning targets. To support this objective, we construct a large-scale pretraining dataset and derive physical state-transition annotations covering task-relevant semantics and visual motion changes, providing more direct supervision for continuous action generation. During inference, the model generates actions directly from current observations without additional inference overhead. VLA-$Δ$ achieves performance competitive with the state of the art on LIBERO and RoboTwin, and outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in real-robot experiments. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-OmniAI/VLA-Delta
candidates.summary_zh: 提出VLA-Δ框架，以当前与未来状态的物理变化为显式监督目标，构建大规模预训练数据与状态转移标注，提升连续动作生成；在LIBERO和RoboTwin具竞争力，真机优于π0.5。
candidates.contribution_zh: 用物理状态转移显式监督VLA，避免仅拟合观测-动作映射；推理无额外开销，并在仿真与真机验证。

candidates.title: Mallea: Building, Steering, and Memorizing Worlds with Coding Agent
candidates.title_zh: Mallea：用编码智能体构建、操控与记忆世界
candidates.abstract: Code world models represent world dynamics through explicit state and executable rules. We investigate how to coordinate object representations, behavioral revisions, and visual memory within this formulation. We present Mallea, a system for building, steering, and memorizing worlds from text. A coding agent infers object interaction requirements from the prompt and jointly plans object structure, properties, and rules, favoring compact representations that support those requirements. The world evolves under the planned rules; optional user actions steer it, while text requests can edit properties or extend capabilities with unaffected state preserved. Object texture memory retains reusable appearance only for whitebox-defined objects and adapts it as those objects change. The program advances world state, while a generative renderer combines current structure with remembered appearance. By organizing construction, intervention, and memory around the same objects, Mallea conditions subsequent observations on the latest state and compatible appearance. Project page: https://lxycopper.github.io/Mallea.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出Mallea系统，利用编码智能体从文本推断物体交互需求，联合规划物体结构、属性与规则，构建可执行代码世界模型；世界按规则演化，用户动作可操控，文本可编辑属性，并保留物体纹理记忆，生成渲染器结合当前结构与记忆外观。
candidates.contribution_zh: 将物体表示、行为修订与视觉记忆统一在代码世界模型中，实现文本驱动的世界构建、交互操控与可复用外观记忆。

candidates.title: Do VLAs Really Follow Instructions? Diagnosing How-Level Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: VLA真的遵循指令吗？诊断视觉-语言-动作模型中的How级指令遵循
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are expected to follow instructions like their language backbones, yet prior work has focused on What-level instructions that specify the task rather than How-level instructions that specify how to carry it out. Through our diagnoses, we find that How-level instructions do not help current VLAs and lower task success. We hypothesize that pairing each training episode with a single instruction limits How-level instruction following, and show that training with segment-level enriched instructions makes actions respond to such instructions without consistently raising task success. To measure How-level instruction following beyond standard benchmarks, we introduce SIMPLER-IN, where success requires conditions given only in the instruction. It shows that the gained responsiveness does not extend to demanding or out-of-distribution How-level instructions. How-level instruction following thus remains an open challenge.
candidates.summary_zh: 论文发现当前VLA模型无法遵循How级指令，提出分段级指令增强训练并引入SIMPLER-IN基准，表明该问题仍是开放挑战。
candidates.contribution_zh: 诊断VLA模型对How级指令的遵循能力，提出分段级指令增强训练，并发布SIMPLER-IN基准。

candidates.title: When to Ask for Help: A Decision-Theoretic Account and Measurement Standard for Slow-Module Scheduling in Dual-System Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: 何时请求帮助：双系统VLA慢模块调度的决策论框架与测量标准
candidates.abstract: Dual-system vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a high-frequency fast policy with a slow, expensive module, and published trigger mechanisms for invoking it lack a shared objective, measured costs, and any standard separating schedule quality from module quality. We provide the missing account: invocation is formalized as a calibrated decision problem whose fixed-ratio, fixed-budget, and history-gated schedules are degenerate cases of one quantity, the Value of Intervention (VoI); a renewal baseline proves the optimal schedule periodic under state-independent collapse, with adaptive gains governed by the cost ratio $ρ$ and the dispersion of collapse. Measured systems span three orders of magnitude in $ρ$ (FiS-VLA $0.95$; RoboICL about $10^3$), and a direct test confirms the low-$ρ$ prediction: calibrated gains vanish under homogeneous collapse and grow with heterogeneity. Fourteen closed-loop arms on LIBERO test the contested middle of the continuum ($ρ=1.53$): the adaptive trigger allocates its queries exactly as the threshold rule predicts, yet the language-rewrite channel cannot convert them into success on either suite, and a revert actuator that undoes a failed rewrite is the only intervention with zero net downside on both LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Goal, where the rewrite deficit deepens from thirteen to forty-two points. A four-measure leak-free protocol cuts apparent early-warning AUC from $0.93$ to $0.62$ on $929$ deployment traces, a detection-limited frontier theorem converts detection quality into a schedulability statement, and a compilation loop turns measured value functions into per-task refresh periods within $2.4\%$ of the closed-loop oracle. Together these results turn slow-module invocation from a design opinion into a measured decision.
candidates.summary_zh: 将双系统VLA慢模块调用形式化为校准决策问题，提出干预价值VoI统一定比例、预算与历史门控调度，并在LIBERO及929条部署轨迹上验证触发、检测与编译循环。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出VoI调度理论、无泄漏四指标评估协议与检测受限可调度性定理，并证明回退执行器是唯一零净损失干预。

candidates.title: KODA: Kinematics--Observation Data Alignment for Humanoid Learning from Human Egocentric Demonstration
candidates.title_zh: KODA：运动学-观测数据对齐用于人类自我中心示范的人形学习
candidates.abstract: Training humanoid whole-body vision-language-action (VLA) policies requires costly robot demonstrations with aligned robot-view observations and controller-compatible whole-body state-action labels. Egocentric human demonstrations offer scalable supervision but have misaligned views and sparse motion cues. Existing approaches either pretrain policies that still require robot data for adaptation or generate controller-specific commands that limit reuse. Conversion also requires robot-view observations aligned with the generated whole-body motion. We present KODA (Kinematics-Observation Data Alignment), which converts egocentric RGB demonstrations into whole-body VLA training data using a reusable canonical trajectory to guide robot-view synthesis and generate controller-specific whole-body state-action supervision. KODA first generates a simulator-checked whole-body trajectory using a sparse tracker with sampling-based command optimization. This generated trajectory directly determines the onboard camera poses used to synthesize corresponding robot-view observations. The motion, observations, and task instruction form a canonical record. For each deployment controller, KODA optimizes commands to track the stored motion and records the corresponding action labels and proprioceptive states. When switching controllers, KODA retains this canonical record and regenerates whole-body state-action supervision for co-training with matching robot demonstrations. We evaluate KODA on four Unitree G1 loco-manipulation tasks using two whole-body controllers, SONIC and HEFT. With robot data held fixed, macro-average success on conditions covered by human demonstrations but absent from robot data improves by 45.0 and 46.25 percentage points, respectively. Under both controllers, this metric shows an upward trend across the evaluated human-data budgets, suggesting potential for further scaling.
candidates.summary_zh: KODA将人类第一视角RGB示范转为全身VLA训练数据：生成模拟器校验轨迹并合成机器人视角观测，为不同控制器生成全身状态动作监督。在Unitree G1上，人演示覆盖但机器人数据缺失时成功率提升超45个百分点。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出运动学-观测数据对齐框架，将人类第一视角示范转换为可复用、控制器兼容的人形全身VLA训练数据，并验证跨控制器可迁移。

candidates.title: Can World and Action Modeling Benefit Each Other under Unified Causal Training?
candidates.title_zh: 统一因果训练下世界建模与动作建模能否相互促进？
candidates.abstract: World and action modeling are closely related, yet their reciprocal benefits under unified causal training remain unclear. We introduce OneWM, a simple framework for unified causal training that treats actions as both conditions for world prediction and targets for policy learning within a shared video-action architecture. Using this framework, we investigate whether learning forward dynamics conditioned on specified actions improves action learning, and whether learning to generate actions in turn improves action-conditioned world modeling. We use LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa365 as embodied testbeds to evaluate both policy learning and world modeling, complemented by real-world policy experiments. Learning the visual consequences of specified actions improves policy performance and generalization across changing scenes. In turn, action learning improves multi-view world-prediction fidelity under the same architecture. Together, these results answer both questions positively, supporting reciprocal benefits between world modeling and action generation under unified causal training.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出OneWM统一因果训练框架，让动作既作世界预测条件又作策略学习目标，在共享视频-动作架构中联合训练。在LIBERO、RoboCasa及真实机器人上验证，二者相互促进，提升策略泛化。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出OneWM统一因果训练框架，验证动作条件世界建模与策略学习可相互促进，并在多类具身基准和真实机器人上验证。

ai_review.reason: 直接研究具身世界模型与动作建模的联合因果训练，并在机器人基准和真机验证，符合收录范围。

candidates.title: EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos
candidates.title_zh: EgoJEPA：超越重定向的自我中心视频灵巧操作
candidates.abstract: Egocentric human videos offer a scalable alternative to costly robot demonstra- tions, yet transferring their manipulation priors to robot control remains chal- lenging. The commonly adopted retargeting-based approaches convert human wrist and finger poses into embodiment-specific action commands through hand- crafted geometric mappings. However, such mappings require meticulous recal- ibration across different embodiments and risk propagating hand-tracking errors into downstream robot control pipelines. To this end, we propose EgoJEPA, a three-stage framework that learns embodiment-agnostic representations from ego- centric human videos without rule-based human-to-robot retargeting: 1) Human- action pre-training learns effect-aware latent actions through JEPA-style visual prediction conditioned on hand-motion differences; 2) Latent-action-based world modeling jointly predicts future visual dynamics and latent actions, which decou- ples human prior pre-training from robot-specific control parameterizations; 3) Embodiment-specific tuning adapts the pretrained model to diverse robots through lightweight action adapters. Experiments on five real-world manipulation tasks across three robot embodiments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of EgoJEPA. It achieves a 74% average success rate under the out-of-domain evalu- ation, compared with 65% for the retargeting baseline, while reducing cumulative cross-embodiment wall-clock cost by 47.2%, from 743.2 to 392.7 hours.

candidates.title: Sign Betting for Misspecified Regression: Variance Adaptivity and Optimal Approximation
candidates.title_zh: 错误设定回归中的符号投注：方差自适应与最优逼近
candidates.abstract: We study bounded regression under model misspecification, evaluating a function $f$ by its $L_1(P_X)$ distance to the conditional mean $η(x)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X=x]$, rather than the standard $L_2(P_X)$. This $L_1$ metric is natural for downstream decision problems such as bandits and reinforcement learning. We analyze the min--max estimator of Baraud & Maillard (2025), which we call \emph{sign-betting regression}. Our main results show that sign-betting regression achieves high-probability $L_1$ oracle inequalities under misspecification. Under realizability, our bound adapts to the average conditional variance and recovers the variance-adaptive rate of Li et al. (2026). We further characterize the optimal universal approximation factor for proper learning by showing that sign betting achieves factor 3, while no proper learner can satisfy a distribution-free, high-probability $L_1$ oracle inequality with a universal approximation factor strictly below 3. We extend the upper-bound analysis beyond finite classes and complement the theory with experiments in synthetic and real-world model-selection tasks.
candidates.summary_zh: 研究模型错误设定下有界回归，以L1距离评估条件均值，分析符号投注极小极大估计的oracle不等式、方差自适应与最优逼近因子，并用于模型选择。
candidates.contribution_zh: 证明符号投注回归在错误设定下达到L1 oracle不等式，刻画最优通用逼近因子为3，并给出方差自适应速率。

ai_review.reason: 统计学习理论，非具身智能或机器人，未涉及物理智能、动作条件建模。

candidates.title: A Phenomenology of Neural Geometry in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.title_zh: 视觉-语言-动作模型中的神经几何现象学
candidates.abstract: Robotic manipulation is inherently geometric, but what shape does the world take inside the policy that performs it? Prior work on vision-language-action (VLA) policies establishes that task-relevant variables are linearly readable from activations, yet readability certifies only that a variable is present and says nothing about the shape its values trace, which may be curved and multi-dimensional. Using controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and activation interventions, we build a taxonomy of seven task-relevant concepts in VLA models. We find that realized geometry is predominantly multi-dimensional and is shaped by the constraints under which the policy acts. Physical joint limits, for example, leave wrist orientation an open arc rather than a circle, and distance to the target, a single scalar, is realized in two orthogonal subspaces, a coarse ruler for the approach and a fine ruler for the grasp. The same geometries reappear in two further VLA models on real-world robot data, indicating that they are neither model-specific nor artifacts of simulation. We demonstrate how the findings are actionable by steering along the geometry a concept realizes. Overall, this work lays out an initial phenomenology of realized geometry in VLA policies and demonstrates that a concept's shape carries as much importance as its readability.
candidates.summary_zh: 通过受控扫描、自然轨迹、线性探针与激活干预，研究VLA策略中七类任务相关概念，发现其实现几何多为多维且受物理约束塑造，并在多个真实机器人数据VLA模型中复现，可沿几何方向操控概念。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出VLA策略中任务相关概念实现几何的分类学，揭示几何形状与可读性同等重要，并展示沿几何方向操控概念的可操作性。

candidates.title: Multi-Dimensional Featurizers Yield Fine-Grained Steering and Data Shaping in Robot Foundation Models
candidates.title_zh: 多维特征器实现机器人基础模型的细粒度引导与数据塑造
candidates.abstract: Can better feature discovery improve control over robot behavior through internal interventions and training data? Recent work in vision and language models reveals multidimensional features, motivating block-sparse featurizers (BSFs), which represent each feature in a low-dimensional subspace. We investigate whether recovering this structure provides an interpretable interface for steering vision-language-action models and shaping the data from which they learn. We show that BSFs recover several multi-dimensional task-relevant features underlying the model's computation (e.g., perception, language, proprioceptive state, episode phase, and control variables). We causally validate these features through fine-grained steering: targeted changes in visual perception, semantic representation, and spatial localization produce predictable changes in downstream action prediction. Finally, we use feature-based data attribution to isolate where a specific behavior (failure recovery) arises in the training dataset, identifying fewer than $1.4\%$ of training tokens whose masking is sufficient to remove the targeted behavior. Overall, our results show how matching featurizers to representation geometry can provide more effective tools for understanding and changing robot behavior.
candidates.summary_zh: 研究块稀疏特征器在VLA模型中恢复多维任务相关特征，并通过细粒度引导验证其对动作预测的因果影响，还用数据归因定位失败恢复行为所需训练数据。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出并验证BSF可解释接口，实现VLA行为细粒度引导，并用特征数据归因定位关键训练token以塑造机器人行为。

ai_review.reason: 面向VLA与机器人基础模型的表征可解释、引导与数据塑造，属具身智能与动作控制。

candidates.title: When Reality Outpaces Cognition: A New Scaling Principle for Reliable Intelligence
candidates.abstract: This paper challenges the understanding capabilities of existing AI paradigms and emerging world models by asking a fundamental question: How quickly can reality change before an intelligent system can no longer reliably perceive, reason, and act? We formulate this as a theory- and model-agnostic challenge in which systems must infer reliable actions for increasingly distant future states across a growing observation--reality gap. We operationalize this challenge through the effective Speed of Coherent Cognition (\(S_C^{\mathrm{eff}}\)), defined as the highest tested Speed of Reality (\(S_R\)) through which a system continuously satisfies a predefined behavioural reliability criterion from baseline. As a proof of concept, reinforcement-learning agents are trained at the baseline \(S_R\) and evaluated, without retraining, as \(S_R\) is increased by up to \(50\times\) while computational resources remain fixed. We compare Transformer and gated-MLP baselines with \(Co^4\), an architecture inspired by cellular mechanisms implicated in conscious processing and awake thought. Across the tested scenarios, \(Co^4\) achieves substantially higher \(S_C^{\mathrm{eff}}\) than the baselines, motivating \(S_C^{\mathrm{eff}}\) as a new benchmark and the scaling of coherent cognition as a principle for reliable AI.

candidates.title: Causal Analysis of Robot Foundation Models Enables Efficiency Gains
candidates.title_zh: 机器人基础模型的因果分析实现效率提升
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are a promising approach to general purpose robot manipulation. While the internal computation of vision-language models, which compose the backbone of VLAs, has been studied extensively, less is known about how their perceptual and semantic representations are transformed into action in VLA models. We study this question mechanistically in three frontier VLA models ($π_{0.5}$, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot) by analyzing the causal pathways through which the input image and the instruction shape actions. Across the three models, activation patching shows that causally relevant information influences the action expert (AE) through a narrow band of mid-to-late cross-attention layers, which we term the action-conditioning interface. The content of this information changes with token and layer within the model. Early-to-mid layer representations of the target noun token determine which object is selected, whereas mid-to-late layers carry the spatial information in text tokens that redirects the movement when patched. Where spatial information is stored in prompt tokens various based on the architecture. In MolmoAct2 the model forms task-conditioned representations at the text positions that follow the instruction, whereas $π_{0.5}$ additionally stores this information at image token positions. We show that these findings can be translated directly into improving model efficiency. We find that restricting MolmoBot's action expert conditioning to only 3 out of 36 layers reduces inference FLOPs by up to $33\%$ while maintaining comparable task success with the default model across 3,000 evaluation episodes ($46.7\%$ vs. $46.9\%$), and the same principle carries over to real-robot deployment of $π_{0.5}$.
candidates.summary_zh: 对三个前沿VLA模型开展机制性因果分析，定位动作条件接口；据此仅保留36层中3层，推理FLOPs降约33%，成功率与默认模型相当。
candidates.contribution_zh: 揭示VLA模型图像与指令影响动作的因果路径，并提出按动作条件接口裁剪层数的高效推理方法。

ai_review.reason: 研究VLA模型因果信息流并提升推理效率，直接服务机器人基础模型，应予收录。

candidates.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
candidates.title_zh: WorldCast：探索世界状态预测中的智能视觉生成
candidates.abstract: Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. We introduce WorldCast, a benchmark comprising 320 manually designed cases across eight categories, and evaluate 12 representative models. The conducted experiments yield three key insights: (a) advances in frontier models are rapidly pushing the boundaries of intelligent world modeling, with the GPT-Image-2.5 System scoring 72.8 and demonstrating early-stage visual state prediction capabilities on real-world tasks; (b) WorldCast reveals substantial gaps between models: even Nano Banana Pro reaches only 42.8 and the best open-source model scores 20.1, with deficits in handling complex context, entangled references, and reasoning-heavy tasks; (c) strong generative models effectively draw on the capabilities of their underlying language models. These findings highlight the need for multimodal generative models that are capable of dynamic planning and reasoning while also being deeply unified to faithfully simulate real-world states.
candidates.summary_zh: 提出WorldCast基准，含320个案例、八类任务，评测12个多模态生成模型的多步世界状态预测能力，发现前沿模型初具视觉状态预测能力但仍存在明显差距。
candidates.contribution_zh: 构建多步世界状态预测基准，揭示多模态生成模型在复杂上下文与推理任务上的能力差距。

ai_review.reason: 多步世界状态预测与动作条件视觉仿真，属世界模型与生成式仿真范畴

candidates.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
candidates.title_zh: Orbia：生成视频能否构成一致的3D世界？
candidates.abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. For generated-content persistence, we compare revisits to regions absent from the input image with their first generated observations to test whether models preserve what they create. For 3D self-consistency, cross-view depth and feature correspondence, regional scale agreement, and held-out Gaussian rendering test whether generated views describe the same 3D scene. Minute-long exploration and revisits further test long-term consistency. Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.
candidates.summary_zh: 介绍Orbia，首个系统评估交互式世界模型3D一致性的基准。从输入保持、生成内容持久性和3D自一致性三个维度评估，涵盖720个实例和27个模型。
candidates.contribution_zh: 提出Orbia基准，系统评估交互式世界模型的3D一致性，涵盖多个维度和协议，为诊断3D不一致性提供基础。
